graph.summary: Sermorelin → Growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor → growth hormone secretion → Pituitary dwarfism

evidence.snippet: GHRH stimulates GH secretion from somatotroph cells of the anterior pituitary via a pathway that involves GHRH receptor activation of adenylyl cyclase and increased cAMP production.
evidence.explanation: Sermorelin is the GHRH(1-29)NH2 agonist; like native GHRH it acts by activating the GHRH receptor, triggering adenylyl cyclase and cAMP signalling.

evidence.snippet: GHRH(1-29)NH2 is equipotent to GHRH(1-40); increasing doses from 10-200 micrograms per subject augments the duration of stimulated growth hormone (GH) release
evidence.explanation: Sermorelin (GHRH(1-29)NH2) is a full GHRH-receptor agonist, equipotent to full-length GHRH in stimulating GH release.

evidence.snippet: The growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor (GHRHR) is a member of the family of G protein-coupled receptors that is expressed on pituitary somatotrope cells and mediates the actions of GHRH in stimulating growth hormone (GH) synthesis and secretion.
evidence.explanation: The GHRH receptor is the somatotroph G-protein-coupled receptor that mediates stimulation of growth hormone secretion.

evidence.snippet: GHRH stimulates GH secretion from somatotroph cells of the anterior pituitary via a pathway that involves GHRH receptor activation of adenylyl cyclase and increased cAMP production.
evidence.explanation: Activation of the GHRH receptor drives the adenylyl-cyclase/cAMP pathway that stimulates GH secretion.

evidence.snippet: We describe a recently identified new form of dwarfism due to isolated growth hormone (GH) deficiency, secondary to inactivating mutations in the GH-releasing hormone receptor (GHRHR) gene.
evidence.explanation: Pituitary dwarfism arises from deficient growth hormone secretion; adequate GH secretion therefore opposes the disease, so raising GH secretion (via sermorelin) nets to reducing dwarfism.

evidence.snippet: Mice homozygous for this mutation have reduced GH secretion and a dwarf phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Loss of GHRH-receptor function reduces GH secretion and produces the dwarf phenotype, confirming the inverse relationship between GH secretion and dwarfism.
